assessments.task_description:
Overview

In this assessment, you will compare a telehealth innovation used in Australia with the same or a similar telehealth innovation implemented in one country of your choice.

A list of telehealth applications is provided below. Select one telehealth application from the list. For each application, an Australian research article has been provided to help you understand the Australian context. You are expected to identify and critically review relevant peer-reviewed research literature relating to the same telehealth application in your chosen comparison country.

Using the evidence you gather, you will compare the two telehealth services and provide a brief analysis of their similarities, differences, and overall effectiveness.

Your report consists of three parts.

Part 1: Introduction (LO1) (300–400 words)

Introduce your chosen telehealth application and provide:

·         A brief description of the telehealth application.

·         The healthcare problem or need that the telehealth innovation addresses.

·         A rationale for selecting this telehealth application.

·         A rationale for choosing your comparison country.

Part 2: Comparison Table (LO2)

Complete the comparison table using evidence from your research.

Use peer-reviewed journal articles and government or policy documents to support your responses.

Do not use news articles, websites, blogs, or other forms of grey literature as sources of evidence.

A table will be provided on Blackboard assessment task portal

Part 3: Comparative Analysis (LO3) (400–500 words)

Based on your comparison, write a critical analysis that addresses the following:

  • The key similarities and differences between the telehealth services in the two countries.
  • How each service improves access to healthcare.
  • The impact of each telehealth innovation on healthcare delivery and patient outcomes, supported by research evidence.
  • Which service appears to be more effective, and why.
  • What lessons one country could learn from the other to improve its telehealth service.

Telehealth Applications

Choose one of the following telehealth applications.

1.       Video consultations

Mathew S, Fitts MS, Liddle Z, Bourke L, Campbell N, Murakami-Gold L, Russell DJ, Humphreys JS, Mullholand E, Zhao Y, Jones MP. Telehealth in remote Australia: a supplementary tool or an alternative model of care replacing face-to-face consultations? BMC Health Services Research. 2023;23:341.

2.       Remote Patient Monitoring

Snoswell CL, Vitangcol KJ, Haydon HM, Gray LC, Leedie F, Smith AC, Caffery LJ. Cost-effectiveness of remote patient monitoring for First Nations peoples living with diabetes in regional Australia. Journal of Telemedicine and Telecare. 2023;29(Suppl 10):3S–7S.

3.       Teledermatology

Xie D, Sullivan J. Teledermatology in Australian public hospital emergency departments: A review. Australasian Journal of Dermatology. 2024;65(6).

4.       Teleradiology

Lindsay D, Bates N, Callander E, Johnston K, Carlisle K, Smith D, Evans R, Larkins S. Evaluating the quality and safety of the BreastScreen remote radiology assessment model of service delivery in Australia. Journal of Telemedicine and Telecare. 2023;29(3):203–210.

5.       Telepathology

Mina A. Setting-Up and Integration of Country Pathology into the Tertiary Medical Facility: Outback Australia as Case Example. Laboratory Medicine. 2006;37(4):219–223.

6.       Teleophthalmology

Razavi H, Copeland SP, Turner AW. Increasing the impact of teleophthalmology in Australia: Analysis of structural and economic drivers in a state service. Australian Journal of Rural Health. 2017;25(1):45–52.

7.       Mobile Health (mHealth) Applications

Byambasuren O, Beller E, Glasziou P. Current knowledge and adoption of mobile health apps among Australian general practitioners: Survey study. JMIR mHealth and uHealth. 2019;7(6).

8.       Telemental Health

Richardson LK, Simpson S. The future of telemental health and psychology in Australia: Restoring the psychologically "clever country". Australian Psychologist. 2015;50(4):307–310.

9.       Telerehabilitation

Ross MH, Simmich J, Lawford BJ, Bennell KL, Hinman RS, Russell T. Telerehabilitation trends in Australian physiotherapy and factors influencing use after COVID-19 restrictions. JMIR Rehabilitation and Assistive Technologies. 2026;13.

10.    Telepharmacy

McFarland R. Telepharmacy for remote hospital inpatients in north-west Queensland. Journal of Telemedicine and Telecare. 2017;23(10):861–865.

Submission Requirements

Word limit: 900–1100 words (excluding the comparison table and reference list).

Submit one Word document containing:

-         Part 1: Introduction

-         Part 2: Completed comparison table

-         Part 3: Comparative analysis

Reference list (APA 7th edition)

Use APA 7th edition for in-text citations and the reference list.

Support your discussion with peer-reviewed literature and government/policy documents.

Write in formal academic language.

assessments.assessment_title: Assessment Task 3: Telehealth Solution Pitch - Recorded presentation
assessments.task_description:
Overview

In this assessment, you will prepare and record a 8 - 10 minute PowerPoint presentation in which you recommend an appropriate telehealth solution for a healthcare service.

You will be provided with a range of healthcare scenarios (available on Blackboard). Select one scenario and develop an evidence-based recommendation for the most appropriate telehealth solution to address the healthcare challenge presented.

Imagine you have been engaged as a digital health consultant. Your role is to advise a healthcare organisation on the most appropriate telehealth solution for the scenario provided. Your recommendation should be evidence-based, practical, and tailored to the needs of the organisation and its patients.

Your presentation should demonstrate how the proposed telehealth solution addresses the identified healthcare need while considering healthcare access, equity, patient outcomes, privacy, security and implementation issues.

Your recommendation should be supported by current research evidence and relevant policy or professional guidance where appropriate.

Presentation requirements

-         Record a 6–8 minute narrated PowerPoint presentation.

-         You must appear on screen during the presentation (e.g., using the presenter view or webcam).

-         Use PowerPoint slides effectively to communicate your ideas. Slides should support your presentation by using appropriate headings, diagrams, figures and limited text rather than large blocks of written content.

-         Present your ideas clearly and professionally using appropriate academic language.

Healthcare scenarios will be available on Blackboard in the Assessment portal.

Your presentation should address the following learning outcomes.

1. Healthcare Problem and Context (LO3)

Analyse the healthcare problem described in your chosen scenario.

Your discussion should include:

·         the nature and significance of the healthcare problem

·         the key stakeholders involved

·         barriers to healthcare access

·         equity considerations

·         the potential impact on patient outcomes

Support your discussion with relevant evidence, statistics and literature.

2. Proposed Telehealth Solution (LO2 & LO3)

Describe and justify the telehealth solution you recommend.

Your discussion should include:

 ·         the telehealth modality (or combination of modalities) proposed

·         how the technology functions within the healthcare setting

·         why this solution is appropriate for the scenario

·         how it addresses the identified healthcare need

Support your justification with evidence from the literature.

3. Impact on Access, Equity and Patient Outcomes (LO3)

Analyse the likely impact of the proposed telehealth solution.

Your discussion should consider:

·         improvements in access to healthcare services

·         implications for health equity

·         effects on patient outcomes and quality of care

·         potential benefits for healthcare providers and the health system, where relevant

Use contemporary evidence to support your analysis.

4. Privacy, Security and Medico-Legal Considerations (LO4)

Evaluate the ethical, legal and professional considerations associated with implementing the proposed telehealth solution.

Your discussion should include consideration of:

·         patient privacy and confidentiality

·         informed consent

·         data security and cybersecurity

·         professional responsibilities

·         relevant legal or regulatory issues

·         potential risks and strategies to minimise them

5. Recommendations (LO4 & LO5)

Provide clear, evidence-based recommendations for adopting and implementing your proposed telehealth solution.

Your recommendations should be:

·         realistic and feasible

·         clearly justified

·         supported by evidence presented throughout your presentation

Your recommendations should address the following questions:

·         What should be done?

·         Why should it be done?

·         What is required for successful implementation? (e.g., technology, workforce training, organisational support, policy, funding or patient engagement)

General Expectations

Your presentation should:

·         demonstrate critical analysis rather than simply describing the telehealth technology

·         integrate evidence from peer-reviewed literature throughout the presentation

·         present a logical and well-structured argument

·         use APA 7th edition referencing for in-text citations and the reference list

·         communicate ideas clearly using professional presentation techniques and well-designed PowerPoint slides

learning_activities.topic:
Module 1: Clinical telehealth - an overview

Covers Weeks 1 - 3 of teaching

It offers a comprehensive understanding of telehealth, encompassing the definition of telehealth, tracing its historical origins and evolution into modern healthcare, and examining both initial and recent benefits.

Module 1 introduces you to how telehealth is linked to ensuring fair access to healthcare for patients, aligning with the Australian Charter of Healthcare Rights, addressing the Quadruple Aim of Healthcare, and contribution to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 3 - Good Health & Well-being.

  • Week 1: What is Telehealth? - What is telehealth and related terms (telemedicine, telecare, e-health and online health), what is clinical telehealth and driver for telehealth  
  • Week 2: Telehealth - the past and the future - History of telehealth and funding related changes since COVID in Australia   
  • Week 3: Benefits of telehealth - Clinical, service and economic benefits of Telehealth, stressing the opportunity to improve access to care      

Refer to the Course 'Learning Resources' on Learn.UQ (Blackboard) for links to all lectures, Weekly Study Guide, required and recommended reading. Content is organised as Module and then by Teaching Week. Content is typically uploaded to Learn.UQ (Blackboard) on the Friday prior to each Teaching Week.


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

learning_activities.topic:
Module 2: Telehealth in action

Teaching Weeks 4-8 explores the different telehealth approaches with respect to delivering healthcare i.e. store and forward models (i.e. asynchronous communication via email, secure messaging, encrypted software,) real-time models (i.e. synchronous communication - video or phone based), mobile-device based models (including remote monitoring/wearables) and hybrid models of care (i.e. a blend of telehealth and face-to-face)

  • Week 4: Approaches to telehealth - an overview - Overview of telehealth briefly explaining all models possible, various classifications and terminologies per specialty
  • Week 5: Telehealth in practice - real-time models - Overview of real-time models, and video and phone consultations
  • Week 6: Telehealth in practice - store and forward models - Overview of store and forward models, teledermatology and eConsults
  • Week 7: Telehealth in practice - mobile health models - Overview of mobile health and potential application for remote patient monitoring
  • Week 8: Telehealth in practice - hybrid models of care - What are models of care, hybrid models, care pathways, the importance of attending to patient needs.

Refer to the Course 'Learning Resources' on Learn.UQ (Blackboard) for links to all lectures, Weekly Study Guide, required and recommended reading. Content is organised as Module and then by Teaching Week. Content is typically uploaded to Learn.UQ (Blackboard) on the Friday prior to each Teaching Week.

Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

learning_activities.topic:
Module 3: Planning & implenting telehealth

Teaching Weeks 9-12 outlines practical considerations, technical requirements, planning for a telehealth program and medico-legal considerations. Week 13 is reserved for review of key concepts covered over the Semester that will assist students with final assessment.

  • Week 9: Planning for telehealth - Telehealth Etiquette and Technology for video conferencing
  • Week 10: Privacy considerations and sustainability of telehealth - Privacy & Security in Telehealth, Sustaining telehealth beyond COVID-19
  • Week 11: Telehealth - future potential - Potential of COVIU, telestroke and Tele-ICU
  • Week 12: Telehealth - a global perspective - Telehealth around the world, including case studies from Denmark, Brazil and Japan
  • Week 13: Review

Refer to the Course 'Learning Resources' on Learn.UQ (Blackboard) for links to all lectures, Weekly Study Guide, required and recommended reading. Weeks 9-12 content will be available from Teaching Week 9 to assist students with final assessment preparation.
